goal: Measure real ROS2/DDS timing jitter around the nominal periods LQI's control loop assumes (5ms /joint_states, 10ms /effort_controller/commands), as a cheap plausibility check before PHYS-002 (closed-loop physics-only harness).

blocker_found_and_fixed.description: In this WSL2 boot session, the shared ros2cli daemon's internal rclpy context reliably dies (RuntimeError: !rclpy.ok(), from ros2cli.node.direct.DirectNode) the moment this project's ROS graph launches -- reproduced 5/5 consecutive attempts, each with a freshly-restarted, confirmed-healthy daemon beforehand. Gazebo itself confirmed fine throughout via gz-transport /clock (bypasses ROS2 entirely). Fixed by adding --no-daemon to the ros2 topic echo/info calls in run_clean_experiment.sh's readiness checks, and replacing the ros2 control list_controllers call (no --no-daemon flag exists for that verb) with a small inline rclpy script calling the ListControllers service directly.
blocker_found_and_fixed.verified_fix: same lqr nominal_balance invocation that failed 5/5 times before now completes end-to-end in ~28s (previously timed out at ~55s every time)

method.recording: measure_jitter.py subscribes to /joint_states and /effort_controller/commands, records time.monotonic() wall-clock arrival for every message plus header.stamp sim-time for joint_states

interpretation.mean_jitter_vs_plan_threshold: By LQI_ROOT_CAUSE_PLAN.md's suggested std thresholds (< 0.5ms negligible, > 2ms clearly significant), mean jitter (std of inter-arrival intervals) falls in between in every run -- mostly 0.35-0.75ms for joint_states, 0.37-0.57ms for commands in 4/5 runs (one outlier run at 1.32ms). Does not clear the '>2ms significant' bar on the std measure alone.
interpretation.worst_case_jitter: p99/max deviation is much larger and not obviously negligible: joint_states max deviation reaches 6.8-9.3ms (up to ~186% of the 5ms nominal period) in 3/5 runs; commands run #4 shows a 9.5ms max deviation on a 10ms nominal period -- essentially a full missed/doubled tick at least once.
interpretation.why_this_could_matter: lqr_node.py's integrator uses a fixed nominal dt (1/rate_hz = 10ms), never actual elapsed wall-clock time, so a single late timer firing (as observed) creates a real one-off integral-state model-mismatch on that step, not something that simply averages out.
interpretation.significance_judgment: explicitly deferred to PHYS-002 per LQI_ROOT_CAUSE_PLAN.md's instruction -- this task reports the measured numbers plainly, does not conclude whether they explain LQI's slow settling

regression_checks.note: only the daemon-dependent internals of the readiness-check helper functions changed; launch order, teardown, and result.json writing are untouched

next_step: PHYS-002 (closed-loop physics-only harness) per LQI_ROOT_CAUSE_PLAN.md Task B
